To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) positive selection and introgressed haplotype frequencies are high in the house mouse, and (ii) introgression is a common process that may contribute to the adaptive landscape of natural populations and may be a factor that needs to be considered when analyzing the genetic basis of phenotypic variation in natural populations and inbred strains of the house mouse.

(1) positive selection acts on rare alleles or new mutations in natural populations of the house mouse, (2) introgression of haplotype blocks is a frequent phenomenon and (3) the introgressed haplotype blocks are often subject to positive selection.
we find a large amount of positive selection in the genomes of natural house mouse populations and that introgressed genomic segments are common.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genomic basis of adaptation in natural populations of the house mouse (Mus domesticus).
the evolution of natural populations and the origin of genetic variation in inbred strains.
evolutionary processes that shape genomes and the resulting adaptive landscape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the house mouse is an excellent model system to investigate patterns of positive selection, introgression, and admixture in natural populations.
the genomes of natural populations of the house mouse are shaped by a complex interplay of positive selection, introgression and recombination.
the house mouse genome is a complex mosaic of positive selection and haplotype introgression, with both processes being of similar importance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genome of natural populations is a mosaic of haplotypes, with introgressed haplotype blocks, regions under positive selection and regions that have been subject to purifying selection.

the genomes of natural populations of mice show a high degree of polymorphism and a large number of selective sweeps, and that a substantial fraction of the genome is affected by haplotype introgression from other populations or subspecies.
the genome is a complex mosaic of introgressed and selected haplotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the house mouse is an ideal model system to study adaptive evolution in natural populations and the role of introgressed alleles.
natural populations are highly polymorphic, and that this polymorphism can be shaped by both positive and negative selection, as well as by introgression from other populations.
the genomes of natural mouse populations have been shaped by a large number of selective sweeps and introgressed alleles.
